name: שְׁאָר יָשׁוּב
summary: Isaiah's son, who went with his father to meet Ahaz at the conduit of the upper pool (Isa 7:3). Isaiah says that he and the children Yahweh had given him are signs in Israel (Isa 8:18), and the boy's name is the sign spelled out three chapters on: “a remnant will return (שְׁאָר יָשׁוּב), the remnant of Jacob, to the mighty God … though your people Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant of them will return” (Isa 10:21–22). It is the noun שְׁאָר “remnant” and יָשׁוּב “will return”, of the root שׁוּב.

evidence.note: “Go out to meet Ahaz, you and Shear-jashub (וּשְׁאָר יָשׁוּב) your son.”
“I and the children whom Yahweh has given me are for signs and wonders in Israel.”
“שְׁאָר יָשׁוּב, the remnant of Jacob, to the mighty God”: the name as a sentence.
“A remnant of them will return”; quoted in Rom 9:27, “the remnant will be saved”.

note: Takes v.ak.ac, which the database counts by the spelling יָשׁוּב (4 tokens, including Jashub of Ezr 10:29 and 1Ch 7:1 and the verb at Psa 73:10); only Isa 7:3 is this name, and the people tag limits the name to him. The שְׁאָר of Isa 7:3 is counted under the noun's key v.ak.ab. יָשׁוּב belongs to the root שוב, which has no entry yet.
